title: Supply and demand in US PCE inflation
methods: The San Francisco Fed classifies individual spending categories each month using price and quantity surprises relative to monthly predictions fitted on rolling ten-year windows. Surprises moving together indicate demand. Opposite movements indicate supply. When either surprise is statistically indistinguishable from zero, the Fed assigns the category to the ambiguous group. A category can change groups over time.

Each monthly observation uses the published trailing twelve-month contribution in percentage points. Headline covers the full PCE basket. Core excludes food and energy. Core contributions use their own basket weights, so subtracting the two panels does not isolate an energy contribution.

The three contributions sum to the decomposition total. The BEA comparison is the percentage change in its seasonally adjusted chain-type price index over twelve months, calculated as 100 × (index / year-earlier index − 1). The accounting gap is BEA inflation minus the contribution sum. It is separate from ambiguous inflation and is retained at its observed sign.

Period means weight each monthly twelve-month observation equally. The change within a period is the last observation minus the first. Adjacent observations share eleven months of underlying data. They cannot be added to obtain the price change over the period.

All dates use a common release vintage for retrospective comparison. Earlier observations can differ from the estimates available at the time. Category classifications describe the joint behaviour of prices and quantities. A reading cannot identify how much a particular fiscal measure, rate decision or supply disruption caused.

panels.label: Headline PCE
findings: From the post-crisis expansion to the 2021–22 reopening, average headline inflation rose 3.84 percentage points. The supply contribution rose 1.80 points, demand 1.32 and ambiguous 0.72.
In March–December 2020 the mean demand contribution was -0.69 points, while supply contributed +1.20. These are twelve-month contributions observed during the shock.
In 2026-09, supply contributed 1.28 points, demand 1.17 and ambiguous categories 1.20. The BEA index rose 3.65% over twelve months.

panels.label: Core PCE
findings: From the post-crisis expansion to the 2021–22 reopening, average core inflation rose 2.85 percentage points. The supply contribution rose 1.19 points, demand 1.15 and ambiguous 0.55.
In March–December 2020 the mean demand contribution was -0.07 points, while supply contributed +0.90. These are twelve-month contributions observed during the shock.
In 2026-09, supply contributed 1.13 points, demand 1.21 and ambiguous categories 0.77. The BEA index rose 3.12% over twelve months.
